categories.label: Kayokyoku / Shōwa Pops
categories.description: The great wellspring of Japanese popular music, developed alongside broadcast and record culture.

categories.label: Folk / New Music
categories.description: Foregrounded self-penned songs and personal lyricism, shaping the singer-songwriter culture that followed.

categories.label: Japanese Folk
categories.description: A movement that changed Japanese song by singing social questions, daily language, and personal stories in artists' own words and music.

categories.label: Ska / Ska Punk
categories.description: A uniquely Japanese dance music built on Jamaican ska, crossing horns, dub, and punk.

categories.label: Japanese Blues / Blues Rock
categories.description: Reinterpreted American blues through Japanese language, dialect, and urban life, building a distinct performance culture centered on the Kansai region.

categories.label: City Pop
categories.description: Fused soul, AOR, and funk with polished arrangements against a backdrop of urban life.

categories.label: Technopop / Electro
categories.description: Brought synthesizers and computers to the center of pop music.

categories.label: Idol Pop
categories.description: A uniquely Japanese pop form uniting song, character, visuals, and fan culture.

categories.label: J-Rock / Band Boom
categories.description: The mainstream of Japanese-language rock, spreading through live houses, television, and festivals.

categories.label: Visual Kei
categories.description: Linked music with costume and stage design, building a distinct aesthetic and influence abroad.

categories.label: Shibuya-kei / Indie
categories.description: Referenced music history from Japan and abroad, showing an urban critical sensibility and DIY spirit.

categories.label: Dance / R&B
categories.description: Club music, R&B, and hip hop advanced to the center of the charts.

categories.label: Hip Hop
categories.description: A culture refining the rhythm and rhyme of Japanese-language rap to depict regional and generational reality.

categories.label: Internet / Vocaloid
categories.description: Music born from video sharing, Vocaloid, and social media, renewing the circuits of creation and listening.

categories.label: Modern J-POP
categories.description: An ongoing pop form freely crossing rock, soul, electronic music, and internet culture.
